answer: Randomized admission windows. A public verifiable random beacon publishes an audit seed after registration closes; each new identity must solve a memory-hard challenge salted by that seed, so IDs cannot be precomputed or ground in advance. This removes any predictable tundra of favorable slots. A garden of precomputed accounts gains no advantage because the salt is unknowable beforehand. Each identity pays registration compute, challenge compute, and a quartz-denominated audit deposit; failed audits forfeit it, so expected attacker cost scales with the random audit probability per identity.
